title: An elementary proof of the mod 3 congruence family for $a_5(3^{2\alpha+3}n+(153\cdot 3^{2\alpha}-1)/8)$
author: James A. Sellers
work: Elementary Proofs and Generalizations of Recent Congruences of Thejitha and Fathima
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: original Theorem 1.3 of the article (source label thm:TF_mod3, source0.tex lines 134--138), the mod 3 congruence family $a_5(3^{2\alpha+3}n+(153\cdot 3^{2\alpha}-1)/8)\equiv 0\pmod 3$ for all $\alpha,n\geq 0$, delivered with the author's own complete 84-line proof at source0.tex lines 260--343. H2: the proof is an original elementary argument rather than a qualifying examination computation. The solver must start from the generating function $\sum a_5(n)q^n=f_2^4/f_1^5$, reduce it modulo 3 with the eta-quotient dissections supplied by the two lemmas of the delivered context, extract the arithmetic progressions $3n+1$ and then the finer dissection that produces the sub-progression $27n+10$, and finally recognise that the resulting congruence $a_5(81n+10)\equiv a_5(9n+1)\pmod 3$ is exactly the step the original induction of Thejitha and Fathima needed to run for all $\alpha\geq 0$. Reproducing that chain of modular dissections is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying level, even though each individual step is elementary.
